steps.name: Install fast-check and build shared arbitrary generators
steps.description: Add fast-check as a dev dependency and define graphArbitrary, nodeArbitrary, edgeArbitrary (causal and constraint variants) at the top of url-encoding.test.ts. Generators must cover the full domain: unicode labels, empty string labels, float coordinates (x/y), float radius, min/max/initial values (with min <= initial <= max), all five SizeTier values (xs/s/m/l/xl), all eight ColourTier values (blue/green/red/orange/yellow/teal/purple/grey), all four DelayLevel values (none/short/medium/long), both polarity values (1 and -1), weight in range 0–5, optional node annotation, optional node role (lever/outcome/undefined), both EdgeKind variants (causal and constraint), both ConstraintKind values (ceiling/floor), empty and non-empty arrays of nodes/edges/annotations/modulators, and modulator polarity (1/-1). No property assertions in this step — generators only.
criteria: fast-check is listed in packages/app/package.json devDependencies
pnpm install succeeds with no audit errors
graphArbitrary, nodeArbitrary, causalEdgeArbitrary, constraintEdgeArbitrary are exported or locally defined at the top of url-encoding.test.ts
Each arbitrary covers its full domain without hardcoded subsets
Running pnpm --filter @swoopy/app test --run exits 0 with all existing tests still green
steps.scenario_name: arbitrary generators are defined and existing tests remain green

steps.name: Roundtrip invariant — decode(encode(g)) deep-equals g
steps.description: Write a property-based test using fc.assert + fc.property(graphArbitrary, g => ...) that asserts deepEqual(decodeGraphFromUrl(encodeGraphForUrl(g)), g) for every valid graph generated by graphArbitrary. The property must use deep structural equality across nodes, edges, annotations, and modulators. No .noShrink().
criteria: fc.assert(fc.property(graphArbitrary, g => { const decoded = decodeGraphFromUrl(encodeGraphForUrl(g)); expect(decoded).toEqual(g); })) passes for the default number of runs
The property exercises graphs with zero nodes, one node, many nodes, all edge kinds, and all optional fields
No .noShrink() is used
All pre-existing tests remain green
steps.scenario_name: property: decode(encode(g)) deep-equals g for any valid graph

steps.name: Idempotency — encode(decode(encode(g))) === encode(g)
steps.description: Write a property-based test asserting that re-encoding a decoded graph produces the same URL string as encoding the original: encodeGraphForUrl(decodeGraphFromUrl(encodeGraphForUrl(g))!) === encodeGraphForUrl(g). This catches serialisation instability where a second encode trip diverges. Only run when decodeGraphFromUrl returns non-null (skip the property iteration otherwise).
criteria: fc.assert(fc.property(graphArbitrary, g => { const once = encodeGraphForUrl(g); const decoded = decodeGraphFromUrl(once); if (decoded === null) return; expect(encodeGraphForUrl(decoded)).toBe(once); })) passes
The property does not use .noShrink()
All pre-existing tests remain green

steps.name: Compression metamorphic — compressed URL is shorter than plain btoa for non-trivial graphs
steps.description: Write a property-based test asserting that for any graph with more than 2 nodes, encodeGraphForUrl(g).length < legacyEncode(g).length, where legacyEncode replicates the plain btoa path (same as the helper already in the test file). This confirms compression is always beneficial at realistic graph sizes.
criteria: fc.assert(fc.property(fc.array(nodeArbitrary, { minLength: 3 }).chain(nodes => fc.record({ nodes: fc.constant(nodes), edges: fc.array(causalEdgeArbitrary, { maxLength: 10 }), annotations: fc.array(annotationArbitrary), modulators: fc.array(modulatorArbitrary) })), g => { expect(encodeGraphForUrl(g).length).toBeLessThan(legacyEncode(g).length); })) passes
The property constrains nodes to minLength: 3 to keep the metamorphic oracle meaningful
No .noShrink() is used
All pre-existing tests remain green
steps.scenario_name: property: compressed URL is shorter than plain btoa for graphs with more than 2 nodes

steps.name: Null safety — decode returns null and never throws for arbitrary strings
steps.description: Write two property-based tests: one over fc.string() and one over fc.base64String(), each asserting that decodeGraphFromUrl(s) returns null without throwing. This guards against exceptions leaking from the inner try/catch in decodeGraphFromUrl.
criteria: fc.assert(fc.property(fc.string(), s => { expect(() => decodeGraphFromUrl(s)).not.toThrow(); expect(decodeGraphFromUrl(s) === null || typeof decodeGraphFromUrl(s) === 'object').toBe(true); })) passes
fc.assert(fc.property(fc.base64String(), s => { expect(() => decodeGraphFromUrl(s)).not.toThrow(); })) passes
No .noShrink() is used
All pre-existing tests remain green
steps.scenario_name: property: decodeGraphFromUrl never throws for arbitrary string inputs

steps.name: Legacy oracle — graphs that round-trip via compressed path also round-trip via legacy uncompressed fallback
steps.description: Write a property-based test confirming that any graph serialisable by encodeGraphForUrl is also recoverable via the legacy plain-btoa path through decodeGraphFromUrl (the fallback branch in the inner try/catch). Use legacyEncode(g) as input to decodeGraphFromUrl and assert deepEqual with the original graph. This proves the legacy fallback path inside decodeGraphFromUrl handles all graphs that the current encoder accepts.
criteria: fc.assert(fc.property(graphArbitrary, g => { const legacy = legacyEncode(g); const decoded = decodeGraphFromUrl(legacy); expect(decoded).toEqual(g); })) passes
The property exercises the fallback branch in decodeGraphFromUrl (plain base64 → JSON.parse path)
No .noShrink() is used
All pre-existing tests remain green
steps.scenario_name: property: graphs round-trip via legacy uncompressed fallback path
